Every ticket in Tessera has one of four statuses.

- **open**: created and waiting for an agent.

reply to reopen the ticket.

ticket linked to it.

A resolved ticket closes automatically after 7 days without a customer reply. Replying to a
resolved ticket within those 7 days moves it back to open, keeping its history and priority.

the SLA article) and the order of the agent queue; it does not change the workflow. Only
agents can change a ticket's priority, and every change is recorded in the ticket history.

The Service runs on a major cloud provider in the European Union, in the Frankfurt and Dublin
regions, each spread over several availability zones.

web endpoints are reachable from the internet, behind a web application firewall and distributed
denial-of-service protection. Databases and internal services accept connections only from the
services that need them.
Infrastructure is defined as code and reviewed like application code. Servers are not changed by

2. Encryption
All customer data is encrypted at rest with AES-256, including databases, file storage for
attachments, search indexes and backups.

data they protect. Keys are rotated every year, and access to the key service is limited to the
automated systems that need it.
Enterprise customers can bring their own key: data is then encrypted with a key held in the
customer's own key vault, and revoking that key makes the workspace's data unreadable.
